description: A newly hired employee whose identity is created and provisioned with birthright access at onboarding; the governance risk is the correctness and timeliness of the initial entitlement grant — over-provisioning at the joiner stage seeds later least-privilege drift.
typical_secrets: Birthright bundle (email, directory, VPN, collaboration suite, baseline business apps); department/role-based entitlements requested via the access-request workflow

description: An existing identity changing role, team, manager, location or employment type; the governance risk is access accretion / privilege creep where movers accumulate prior-role entitlements that are never removed — the single most common audit finding.
typical_secrets: Old-role plus new-role entitlements concurrently (the defect); should be net of removed prior-role access

description: A departing employee (resignation, termination, end of contract); governance risk is timely complete de-provisioning across all systems, especially federated SaaS and standing tokens that survive directory disable.
typical_secrets: All access from the active lifecycle pending revocation; residual risk in SaaS sessions, OAuth refresh tokens and cached credentials

description: Non-employee workforce — contractors, consultants, outsourced run teams, partner/vendor staff with internal access; governance risk is sponsorship and time-bounding, as these identities lack an HR feed and default to no automatic leaver event.
typical_secrets: Scoped project access, often privileged remote access; frequently no defined expiry

description: A workforce identity holding high-impact business entitlements (not infrastructure admin, which is PAM's domain) — e.g. payments approver, bulk customer-data export, fraud-override, GL-posting, core-banking / ERP super-user; governance risk is the frequency and rigour of recertification and SoD enforcement.
typical_secrets: Business super-user / maker-checker-override roles, bulk data access, financial transaction authority

description: A governance role (not an end-user access pattern): the accountable owner of an application/system who must approve access requests to it and attest its entitlement model; governance risk is ownership coverage and currency — orphaned applications with no owner cannot be governed or certified.
typical_secrets: Approval authority over the app's entitlements; data-classification accountability; recertification-campaign respondent

description: The governance role accountable for a business or technical RBAC role definition — its membership rules, contained entitlements and SoD constraints; governance risk is role hygiene (stale definitions, role explosion, roles silently bundling toxic combinations).
typical_secrets: Authority to define/modify role contents and membership criteria; role-recertification respondent

description: A workforce identity holding entitlements that are individually legitimate but collectively toxic under SoD — e.g. vendor-master maintenance plus payment-run, or journal-entry plus journal-approval; the SOX/ICFR-critical class where the assessment must detect SoD conflicts, not just provision access.
typical_secrets: Conflicting financial-process entitlements (P2P, O2C, R2R, treasury); mitigated by compensating controls where conflicts are accepted

description: A non-human / functional account that IGA governs as a first-class object — with a named human owner, defined purpose, recertification and a de-provisioning trigger — rather than leaving it to PAM/secrets vaulting alone; the governance defect is ownerless, never-recertified, never-expiring service accounts.
typical_secrets: Application-to-application access, batch/integration privileges, often standing and over-scoped

description: Any identity receiving access automatically by virtue of an attribute (department, job code, location) via birthright policy or RBAC assignment with no per-request approval; governance risk is over-broad birthright scope that grants too much by default and is rarely re-examined.
typical_secrets: Attribute-driven default bundles; RBAC role memberships

description: An account that is dormant (unused beyond a threshold) or orphan (no valid owner/identity behind it — e.g. survived a leaver, or a service account whose owning app was decommissioned); the highest-value attestation finding class and a prime lateral-movement target. Both a class and a KPI: a low population is evidence JML, service-account and consent-grant governance work.
typical_secrets: Whatever the account last held — rarely re-reviewed, often still privileged

description: An LLM-driven autonomous agent that calls functions/tools and acts on systems with delegated agency on behalf of a user or business process; a new governed object needing an owner, scoped recertified entitlement set, purpose, least-privilege tool access, human-in-the-loop gates on irreversible actions and a de-provisioning trigger. Dynamic permission change defeats classic point-in-time recert, so model continuous attestation as the good end-state.
typical_secrets: Tool/extension scopes, downstream API permissions, often inherited via an over-privileged service account or an OAuth session broader than the task requires

description: A registered OAuth application / service principal operating against tenant data under delegated or admin-consented scopes, plus the standing consent grants themselves as governed objects (the Midnight-Blizzard pattern); governance risk is over-scoped, un-owned, never-recertified consent that confers durable account-independent access surviving the JML of any human who created it. Model continuous attestation as the good end-state.
typical_secrets: Delegated/application OAuth scopes (Graph, Exchange full_access_as_app, etc.), refresh tokens, app-role assignments — frequently far broader than function requires
